categories.name: Comparative evaluation against alternatives
categories.definition: Designs whose main output is a ranking of the proposed method or model against named competitors on shared tasks.
categories.include_if: The independent variable is which method or model is used, and the claim is about which one is better.
categories.exclude_if: Competitors differ only by removing one internal component of the proposed method (use component-attribution), or the point is transfer to a new setting (use generalization-transfer).

categories.name: Multi-benchmark head-to-head table
categories.definition: The proposed method and published baselines are run on several standard datasets or metrics and reported in one main table.
categories.include_if: There are several baselines and several datasets or metrics, and no explicit matching of budget or cost.
categories.exclude_if: Compute, tokens or parameters are explicitly equalised (budget-matched-comparison), or the method is evaluated along a sweep of cost (quality-cost-frontier).

categories.name: Budget- or capacity-matched comparison
categories.definition: Methods are compared with compute, tokens, simulator calls, parameters or unique data held equal, so the gain cannot be blamed on extra resources.
categories.include_if: The design explicitly equalises a resource, or adds a capacity-matched control to rule out 'it is just bigger'.
categories.exclude_if: The resource is swept continuously and a frontier is plotted (quality-cost-frontier).

categories.name: Quality-versus-cost frontier sweep
categories.definition: Methods are traced across a range of budgets, compression rates or step counts to compare whole trade-off curves or Pareto fronts.
categories.include_if: The x-axis is a resource (bitrate, steps, time, tokens, particles) and every method is plotted along it.
categories.exclude_if: Only the proposed method is swept, to find its own operating point (hyperparameter-sensitivity-sweep).

categories.name: Many-model benchmark leaderboard
categories.definition: A new benchmark or attack is applied to many existing models in order to characterise the field, not to promote one method.
categories.include_if: The paper contributes a benchmark, dataset or attack, and the rows are off-the-shelf models.
categories.exclude_if: The rows include a proposed method that is meant to win (multi-benchmark-head-to-head).

categories.name: Human preference or side-by-side qualitative comparison
categories.definition: Outputs of competing methods are judged by people (pairwise preference, expert ratings) or shown side by side in curated visual comparisons.
categories.include_if: The evidence is human judgments or curated visual galleries comparing methods.
categories.exclude_if: People are used to validate a metric or a judge rather than to compare methods (measurement-validity).

categories.name: Component attribution
categories.definition: Designs that credit a gain to specific parts of the proposed method by removing, adding or replacing them.
categories.include_if: The method's own internals are varied and the claim is 'component X is responsible'.
categories.exclude_if: The varied quantity is a continuous knob (robustness-sensitivity), or the intervention targets the activations of a trained network (mechanistic-analysis).

categories.name: Leave-one-out component ablation
categories.definition: Each module, loss term or reward is removed from the full system in turn, and the drop is measured.
categories.include_if: The design is 'full method minus X' for one or more X, starting from the full system.
categories.exclude_if: Components are added cumulatively from a base (additive-buildup-ablation), or X is replaced by a specific alternative (component-substitution).

categories.name: Cumulative build-up ablation
categories.definition: Components or training stages are added one at a time to a baseline, and the increment from each is reported.
categories.include_if: The table rows build up from a base toward the full method, or add modules onto external baselines.
categories.exclude_if: The design starts from the full system and removes parts (leave-one-out-ablation).

categories.name: Component substitution / design-choice swap
categories.definition: A design choice is swapped for named alternatives (latent space, masking rule, selection criterion, objective form), keeping everything else fixed.
categories.include_if: Each condition replaces one choice with another concrete option, not with nothing.
categories.exclude_if: The swapped part is outside the method (judge, backend, reward model), so the question is robustness (evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap).

categories.name: Confound-isolating control
categories.definition: A control condition separates the claimed cause from a plausible confound: the same data under SFT versus RL, an oracle input, interaction versus static examples, or a matched random subspace.
categories.include_if: The question is phrased as 'is it X or merely Y?' and one condition removes X while keeping Y.
categories.exclude_if: It is a plain removal with no named rival explanation (leave-one-out-ablation).

categories.name: Robustness and sensitivity
categories.definition: Designs that check whether a conclusion survives changes to knobs, inputs or the evaluation setup.
categories.include_if: The claim is stability ('still holds', 'insensitive to'), not improvement.
categories.exclude_if: The change is to the domain, dataset or backbone (generalization-transfer).

categories.name: Hyperparameter sensitivity sweep
categories.definition: One method's own hyperparameter (β, depth, step size, threshold, K) is swept to show a stable range or an optimum.
categories.include_if: Only one method's configuration varies along a scalar knob.
categories.exclude_if: The knob is model or data scale and the goal is a trend or law (scaling-and-extrapolation), or competitors are plotted along the knob (quality-cost-frontier).

categories.name: Input perturbation / corruption stress test
categories.definition: Inputs or side information are corrupted on purpose (noise, JPEG, attacks, label masking, swapped partitions, paraphrased prompts) at graded severity.
categories.include_if: A controlled degradation is applied to inputs or supervision, and performance retention is measured.
categories.exclude_if: The shift is a different natural dataset or domain (cross-dataset-replication).

categories.name: Evaluator, seed and infrastructure stability
categories.definition: Something outside the method is varied (judge model, reward model, scoring rule, random seed, black-box solver, number of runs) to check that rankings or fits are stable.
categories.include_if: The varied element is part of the measurement or execution pipeline, not the method.
categories.exclude_if: The varied element is a design choice of the method (component-substitution).

categories.name: Generalization and transfer
categories.definition: Designs that move a trained model or a method to conditions it was not developed on.
categories.include_if: The question is 'does it still work there?' for a new dataset, domain, backbone, length or task.
categories.exclude_if: The degradation is synthetic and graded (input-perturbation-stress-test).

categories.name: Cross-dataset / cross-domain replication
categories.definition: The main comparison is re-run on another dataset, domain or real-world setting to show the result replicates.
categories.include_if: The method and baselines stay the same, and the data or domain changes.
categories.exclude_if: The architecture or backbone changes (cross-backbone-transfer), or the model is trained on one split and tested zero-shot on another (held-out-split-extrapolation).

categories.name: Cross-backbone / cross-architecture transfer
categories.definition: The method is applied unchanged to a different base model, backbone, generator family or system scale.
categories.include_if: The base model or architecture is swapped while the method stays fixed.
categories.exclude_if: The new setting is a different task family (module-transplant).

categories.name: Train-on-one, test-on-unseen split
categories.definition: Training is restricted to one source (a dataset, sequence length, opponent set or model type), and evaluation is on held-out conditions.
categories.include_if: The train and test conditions are explicitly disjoint by design, including length extrapolation.
categories.exclude_if: The method is simply re-run end-to-end on another dataset (cross-dataset-replication).

categories.name: Module transplant into another system or task
categories.definition: One proposed ingredient is inserted into a different model or a different task to show it is a general improvement.
categories.include_if: A single component, not the whole method, is ported to a foreign host.
categories.exclude_if: The whole method moves to a new backbone (cross-backbone-transfer).

categories.name: Scaling and extrapolation
categories.definition: Designs that vary scale (model, data, compute, input size) to estimate trends, laws or asymptotic cost.
categories.include_if: Scale is the independent variable, and the claim concerns a trend or exponent.
categories.exclude_if: Scale is just a budget axis for comparing methods (quality-cost-frontier).

categories.name: Scale sweep for trend or optimum
categories.definition: Model size, data amount, generation length, batch size or task count is swept to reveal a trend or a scale-dependent optimum.
categories.include_if: The sweep is over a size or amount, and the claim is how the outcome changes with it.
categories.exclude_if: A parametric fit is used to predict unseen scales (fit-and-extrapolate).

categories.name: Fit early, predict later
categories.definition: A functional form is fitted on small or early runs and checked against held-out larger or later runs.
categories.include_if: A fitted curve is evaluated on scales it was not fitted on.
categories.exclude_if: The curve is only descriptive (scale-trend-sweep).

categories.name: Resource cost vs problem size profiling
categories.definition: Runtime, memory or overhead is measured as input size grows, or under deployment engines, to establish efficiency.
categories.include_if: The outcome is wall-clock, memory or FLOPs rather than quality.
categories.exclude_if: Quality is plotted against cost for several methods (quality-cost-frontier).

categories.name: Synthetic settings and theory validation
categories.definition: Designs that use constructed environments where the ground truth or a theoretical prediction is known.
categories.include_if: The data or environment is built so that the right answer is known in advance.
categories.exclude_if: Real data with graded corruption (input-perturbation-stress-test).

categories.name: Simulation vs theoretical prediction overlay
categories.definition: Empirical curves from controlled simulations are overlaid on the predicted rates, bounds or equilibria across parameter sweeps.
categories.include_if: A theorem's quantitative prediction is plotted against measurements.
categories.exclude_if: The theory is only qualitatively illustrated with a constructed case (constructed-counterexample).

categories.name: Constructed toy counterexample
categories.definition: A minimal hand-built environment or graph exhibits a predicted failure or disagreement.
categories.include_if: A single designed instance proves existence (policies disagree, work blows up, the update fails).
categories.exclude_if: The result is a parametric sweep against a prediction (theory-prediction-overlay).

categories.name: Planted ground-truth recovery
categories.definition: Known signals (real images among synthetic ones, true inputs among noise, an exact conjugate posterior) are planted, and recovery is scored.
categories.include_if: Success is measured against a planted target the method does not see.
categories.exclude_if: The ground truth is a theoretical rate rather than a planted object (theory-prediction-overlay).

categories.name: Mechanistic / internal analysis
categories.definition: Designs that look inside trained models or optimisation dynamics to explain why a method works.
categories.include_if: The measured objects are representations, attention, gradients, routing or loss variance.
categories.exclude_if: Only outputs are categorised (behavioral-diagnostics).

categories.name: Probing and representation similarity
categories.definition: Linear probes, CCA or RSA, or classifiers on activations measure what information representations encode or how similar they are.
categories.include_if: The output is a readout or similarity score computed from frozen activations.
categories.exclude_if: Activations are edited and behaviour is re-measured (causal-internal-intervention).

categories.name: Causal intervention on internals with matched controls
categories.definition: A subspace, head or update component is erased, restored or amplified, and the behavioural effect is compared with matched random controls.
categories.include_if: Internal states are edited at inference or in the optimiser, and the downstream effect is measured.
categories.exclude_if: Whole modules of the method are removed and the model is retrained (leave-one-out-ablation).

categories.name: Visualizing learned internals over training
categories.definition: t-SNE or PCA, attention maps, routing traces or learned weight maps are plotted to show qualitative structure or how it evolves.
categories.include_if: The evidence is mainly a visualization of internal quantities, without an intervention.
categories.exclude_if: A quantitative probe or a statistical test is the main evidence (representation-probing).

categories.name: Verify the method moves its target quantity
categories.definition: The method is checked to change the intermediate quantity its motivation names (gradient variance, redundant tokens, alignment score, smoothness).
categories.include_if: The outcome is the mediator posited by the method or theory, not the end metric.
categories.exclude_if: The mediator is correlated across many checkpoints without the method being applied (metric-outcome-correlation).

categories.name: Behavioral diagnostics of outputs
categories.definition: Designs that characterise when and how systems fail by slicing or probing their outputs.
categories.include_if: The analysis is on outputs or trajectories and explains strengths or weaknesses.
categories.exclude_if: The analysis inspects internal activations (mechanistic-analysis).

categories.name: Failure-mode categorization
categories.definition: Errors or reasoning traces are coded (manually or by an LLM) into a taxonomy, and their frequencies are compared.
categories.include_if: The output is a distribution over error or behaviour categories.
categories.exclude_if: Performance is broken down by input attributes rather than by error type (stratified-breakdown).

categories.name: Stratified performance breakdown
categories.definition: The score or gain is split by difficulty, domain, density, stage or a context factor to find where effects concentrate.
categories.include_if: The same results are re-sliced by an input attribute.
categories.exclude_if: New inputs are constructed to create the strata (controlled-input-injection).

categories.name: Controlled input injection probe
categories.definition: Crafted content (distractors, partial guidance, attack payloads, decomposition prompts) is inserted into inputs to test a specific behavioural capacity.
categories.include_if: The inputs are deliberately constructed to elicit and measure one behaviour.
categories.exclude_if: The goal is graded robustness to generic noise (input-perturbation-stress-test).

categories.name: Qualitative case study / post-mortem
categories.definition: A small number of trajectories, incidents or attacks are walked through in detail and mapped to explanatory principles.
categories.include_if: The evidence is narrative analysis of a few instances.
categories.exclude_if: The instances are aggregated into counts (failure-taxonomy).

categories.name: Measurement validity and data audits
categories.definition: Designs that check the measuring instrument itself (metrics, judges, datasets, leakage) before relying on it.
categories.include_if: The object being evaluated is the metric, judge, detector, dataset or a contamination risk.
categories.exclude_if: Evaluator swaps that only test ranking stability (evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap).

categories.name: Metric or judge agreement with human or ground truth
categories.definition: Automatic metrics, LLM judges or pipeline detectors are correlated with human labels or held-out ground truth.
categories.include_if: The output is an agreement or correlation statistic for an evaluator.
categories.exclude_if: A theory-motivated mediator is correlated with performance (targeted-quantity-check).

categories.name: Leakage, contamination and shortcut control
categories.definition: The design tests whether results come from answer leakage, memorisation, self-sampling bias or shortcut questions.
categories.include_if: A named contamination path is measured or removed.
categories.exclude_if: A confound inside the method's own mechanism is isolated (confound-isolating-control).

categories.name: Dataset characterization and audit
categories.definition: Descriptive statistics, difficulty comparisons or manual audits establish the properties and quality of a dataset.
categories.include_if: The subject of the experiment is a dataset, not a model.
categories.exclude_if: Models are scored on the dataset (many-model-leaderboard).

unused_or_rare: safety-fairness-privacy (1 use, neurips26-3178/e5; the security papers neurips26-1214 and neurips26-8717 are not tagged with it)
human-evaluation as a manipulation (about 6 uses; it is a measurement mode, not a manipulation)
overlapping_pairs: Batch size, walker count, generation budget and context limit are assigned to either label inconsistently (iclr26-1322/e7 vs iclr26-0731/e3 vs iclr26-4047/e6).
Swapping one design choice for a named alternative is tagged 'ablation' in iclr26-1692/e4 but 'method-vs-baselines' in neurips26-7100/e6 and neurips26-8717/e4.

'Why does X help' questions get either label or both (iclr26-3769/e4, icml26-5933/e5) without a rule; attribution should mean credit to a component, and mechanism should mean an explanation via internal or causal process.
Dataset replications and backbone swaps are tagged with either label (icml26-4959/e8, neurips26-7079/e3).
Planted signals and constructed distortions are split between the two labels (iclr26-2940/e6 vs neurips26-7100/e7).
missing: A 'budget-matched' or 'capacity-control' label that is used consistently; it currently appears on only about 12 items, though many more designs are matched.
A 'confound control' or 'oracle/upper-bound' manipulation (neurips26-1707/e3, iclr26-1692/e3, neurips26-6504/e5).
'Evaluator swap' or 'seed variance' as a manipulation, separate from ablation.
'Transfer' manipulations: new backbone, new dataset, held-out split.
An 'input injection / adversarial construction' manipulation (distractors, attacks).
'Stratification / post-hoc slicing' as an analysis mode, distinct from pure observational work.

A claim type for 'measurement validity' (a metric or judge is trustworthy); this is currently forced into mechanism (neurips26-3178/e2) or comparative-performance (neurips26-3264/e5, neurips26-5220/e4).
axis_problems: comparative-performance is over-assigned. It is attached to about 45% of items, including transfer, robustness and mechanism-check experiments where it is secondary (e.g. iclr26-2940/e6, neurips26-3488/e6).

method-vs-baselines is used as a catch-all for any comparison of conditions, including leaderboards of off-the-shelf models, detector comparisons and before/after comparisons (neurips26-3264/e1, neurips26-8717/e3).
observational conflates descriptive dataset statistics, correlation analyses, visualizations and case studies, which are very different designs.
The 'ablation' manipulation is often paired with hyperparameter-sweep on the same item (iclr26-1185/e7, icml26-1148/e5), which shows the axis is multi-label without a primary/secondary distinction.

Some labels look misassigned: claim 'comparative-performance' with manipulation 'observational' on detector validation (neurips26-5220/e4), and 'internal-intervention' on before/after RL attention maps (iclr26-1185/e1).

notes: I could not tally all 401 items one by one, so the counts are best-effort estimates; check them before relying on them. Family nodes are set to count 0 so that only leaf counts sum toward the total (≈399 assigned, 2 uncovered). Designs differ more by what is held fixed than by what is varied. A third v0 axis, 'control' (matched budget, matched random subspace, oracle, capacity-matched, same data), would capture design rigour far better than the current manipulation labels. The claim_type axis should be restricted to one primary label plus an optional secondary, because annotators currently stack two or three labels that mirror the manipulation (method-vs-baselines → comparative-performance). The role field (main/ablation/analysis/sanity/appendix) correlates strongly with the taxonomy families and could be used as a weak prior for auto-labelling. Benchmark and attack papers (neurips26-7781, neurips26-1214, neurips26-8717) use a distinct design vocabulary (leaderboards, failure taxonomies, case studies) that v0's method-centric labels underserve.
